blocks.text: Classes of malnutrition are severe wasting and/or nutritional oedema and moderate wasting
Table 24.7: Classification and Diagnostic Criteria of Acute Malnutrition in Children
Presence of bilateral pitting oedema of feet AND/OR
Infant fails to gain weight or loses >10% of initial weight
Nutritional oedema of any grade AND/OR
Weight-for-Height Z-score (WHZ) / Weight-for-Length Z-score (WLZ) < -3 SD AND/OR
MUAC ≥11.5 cm to <12.5 cm (115–124 mm) AND
For children 6–59 months: MUAC ≥115 mm and <125 mm
AND/OR presence of bilateral pitting oedema
MUAC = Mid-Upper Arm Circumference, WHZ = Weight-for-Height Z-score, WLZ = Weight-for-Length Z-score
Note: Nutritional oedema automatically classifies the child as Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) regardless of anthropometric measurements.

Reduced fat and muscle tissue may be masked by oedema
May be less visible due to oedema
Marked muscle wasting with “old man” appearance
Muscle wasting may be present but less obvious
Bilateral pitting oedema beginning in feet/lower legs and may progress to trunk, face, hands, and arms

blocks.text: Table 24.9 Summary of medical complications and danger signs
No appetite or unable to eat
Hypothermia (Axillary Temperature <35.5C, Rectal Temperature <36.5 C) High fever (≥38.5 C)
Cough and fast breathing (as per IMCI guidelines) ;Lower chest in-drawing
Severe dehydration based on recent history of fluid loss (watery diarrhoea/vomiting) with weight loss
Extremely weak and lethargic, unconscious, fitting/convulsions
All children with complicated wasting and/or nutritional oedema are at risk of complications or death.
Stabilize before referral and Refer urgently.
